headline: Highest risk is medium: Plane can ingest files and broad network egress creates leakage/cascade paths, while prompt-injection and capability conflict are limited by the profiles.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven. However, Plane accepts file uploads and hyperlinks, and if awesome-nlp content is manually copied or uploaded into Plane, instruction-like text could be misread. awesome-nlp itself has no I/O surfaces, so the bridge is indirect and user-mediated.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is copied into Plane file uploads or notes
IF Plane parses uploaded text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Do not upload untrusted text from awesome-nlp into Plane
Use a review step before any Plane task consumes copied content
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches files, notes, issues, and hyperlinks and has broad network egress, so sensitive content placed into it can leave the local boundary. awesome-nlp has no documented data classes or egress, so the main leakage path is through Plane’s default external connectivity rather than a symmetric pairwise share.
conditions: IF sensitive files or notes are imported into Plane
IF Plane sends those contents to external services over its broad egress
mitigations: Restrict Plane egress at the network layer
Use a separate redacted workspace for imported content
Review file-upload permissions before enabling them
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound requests

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or network surfaces, while Plane explicitly lacks filesystem write and only supports multiple instances. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is operational overlap through shared human workflows, which is smaller than the rubric’s medium threshold.
conditions: IF both agents are manually pointed at the same mutable external resource
IF an operator treats Plane outputs as edits to a shared system
mitigations: Keep Plane and awesome-nlp on separate resources
Avoid using either agent as the sole editor of shared state
Assign one agent read-only roles where possible

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can act on issues, tasks, and notes, so if it consumes outputs derived from awesome-nlp without verification, errors can cascade into downstream work products. awesome-nlp is a static list and does not verify facts or provide action gating, so the pair lacks a built-in correction loop.
conditions: IF Plane uses text derived from awesome-nlp as authoritative task input
IF no human verification step checks the imported content before scheduling or issue creation
mitigations: Require human review before Plane creates tasks from imported text
Cross-check imported claims against source links
Limit Plane automation to draft mode
requires-engineering: add validation rules for imported content

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a compliance breach is not established. Plane’s file uploads and external APIs could create policy issues if regulated data is introduced, but awesome-nlp has no documented sensitive-data handling and no direct compliance surface is cited.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane
IF the operator requires residency or retention controls that Plane is not configured to enforce
mitigations: Do not store regulated data in Plane
Use a separate tenant for regulated projects
